chapter: Washington clubs, Louis Jordan and Sarah Vaughan, 1949-54
title: Jimmy Jones returns and he is out of work again
summary: When Sarah takes a summer 1954 vacation Jimmy Jones recovers and resumes his chair, so Malachi returns to Washington and organizes his own jobs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Anyway, around the first of the summer of 1954, we played

an engagement at some beach in Maryland, I think, and it was decided that Sarah was going to take a vacation (actually, I think this was around the middle of the summer) and was not going to start back until September. During that time, Jimmy Jones, who had been hospitalized when I took the job, came out of the hospital. He was well and healthy, and he came back to his job.

So then, again, I was in Washington without a job, and so it meant I started working in clubs, in one thing or another. I think during that time, any time I had a job almost it was one I organized and got myself, by having a trio or a band or some kind of.... It's kind of funny. If you get into a situation like that, where you are a bandleader for any length of time, it seems as if the only time you ever get a job or anybody ever calls you for a job is... As a matter of fact, no one ever calls you. Any job that you ever get, you usually wind up getting it yourself.
